title: Problem 06
markdown:
### Problem
The quadrilateral $ABCD$ is partitioned into four triangles by means of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. The areas of three of the triangles are indicated in the diagram: $\text{Area}(APD) = 80, \text{Area}(ABP) = 150, \text{Area}(CBP) = 180$, where $P$ is the intersection of the diagonals. What is the area of the quadrilateral?

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2018-p06](study/assets/asset-heuer-2018-p06-heuer-2018-p06.png)

### Solution (adapted from the official solution)
The area of $ABCD$ is 506.

![Figure for Jerry Heuer heuer-2018-p06-solution](study/assets/asset-heuer-2018-p06-solution-heuer-2018-p06-solution.png)

Let $P$ be the intersection of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$.

Triangles $\triangle APD$ and $\triangle CPD$ share the common altitude from $D$ to diagonal $AC$, so their areas are proportional to the segments of $AC$:

$$\frac{\text{Area}(\triangle APD)}{\text{Area}(\triangle CPD)} = \frac{AP}{CP}.$$

Similarly, triangles $\triangle ABP$ and $\triangle CBP$ share the common altitude from $B$ to diagonal $AC$, so:

$$\frac{\text{Area}(\triangle ABP)}{\text{Area}(\triangle CBP)} = \frac{AP}{CP}.$$

Equating these two expressions:

$$\frac{\text{Area}(\triangle APD)}{\text{Area}(\triangle CPD)} = \frac{\text{Area}(\triangle ABP)}{\text{Area}(\triangle CBP)}.$$

Substituting the given values $\text{Area}(\triangle APD) = 80$, $\text{Area}(\triangle ABP) = 150$, $\text{Area}(\triangle CBP) = 180$:

$$\frac{80}{\text{Area}(\triangle CPD)} = \frac{150}{180} = \frac{5}{6}.$$

Solving for $\text{Area}(\triangle CPD)$:

$$\text{Area}(\triangle CPD) = 80 \times \frac{6}{5} = 96.$$

The total area of quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the four triangular areas:

$$\text{Area}(ABCD) = 150 + 180 + 80 + 96 = 506.$$

### Conceptual Explanation
In any convex quadrilateral with diagonals intersecting at $P$, opposite triangular products are equal: $\text{Area}(ABP) \times \text{Area}(CDP) = \text{Area}(ADP) \times \text{Area}(BCP)$. Thus $150 \times \text{Area}(CDP) = 80 \times 180 \implies \text{Area}(CDP) = 96$. Total area = $150 + 180 + 80 + 96 = 506$.

### Key Technique
Opposite diagonal area product identity $A_1 A_3 = A_2 A_4$ in convex quadrilaterals.
